document_meta.title: BOLT, HEX HEAD, CLOSE TOLERANCE, 6AL-4V TITANIUM ALLOY, SELF-LOCKING AND NONLOCKING
document_meta.issuer: National Aerospace Standard / Aerospace Industries Association of America
document_meta.completeness_warning: Sheet 5 of 5 is MISSING from this file. Nothing extracted here lives on sheet 5, but no consumer may assume this document is complete.

entries.subject: NAS6403 thru NAS6420
entries.note: Criteria and definitions that apply across the whole standard, separated from the per-part-number dimensions so a stack citing one bolt does not have to re-read the family rules. Columns J and N are printed in the sheet-1 table and are never defined in words anywhere in the document; they were deliberately NOT extracted rather than guessed. N is also printed with the SMALLER value on top (.18 over .20 for NAS6403), the opposite of every other two-value column on that sheet, which is a second reason not to assume its meaning.

part_number_code.text: Dash number indicates grip in .0625 increments. Add "A" after basic part number for aluminum coating. Add "D" after dash number for drilled shank. Add "H" after dash number for drilled head. Add "L" after basic part number for self-locking bolts, optional configuration. Add "U" after basic part number for unplated bolts. Add "P" after basic part number for self-locking bolts, patch type.
part_number_code.note: This is what settles, FROM THE PART NUMBER ALONE, that NAS6403U11D is an unplated, drilled-shank bolt -- i.e. that the joint it appears in is cotter-retained through the shank. No drawing is needed for that claim.

at.note: CODE block; restated in the sheet-3 footnote

grip_increment.note: Sheet 3 footnote: "Nominal grip dimension equals grip dash number times .0625 (rounded to 3 decimal places)." Checks: dash 11 -> .6875 -> .688 tabulated; dash 13 -> .8125 -> .812 tabulated.

grip_definition.text: Grip-length of bolts shall be measured from the underside of head to the end of the full cylindrical portion of the shank.
grip_definition.note: The definition the sheet-3 grip column tabulates. A stack element for grip means THIS length and no other.

reference_dimension_meaning.text: Reference dimensions are for design purposes only, not an inspection requirement.
reference_dimension_meaning.note: What makes T a reference: it is not independently controlled, so folding a band on T alongside bands on grip and length double-counts.

nominal_length_rule.text: Intermediate and longer lengths may be specified by use of whole grip dash numbers only. Nominal grip dimension equals grip dash number times .0625 (rounded to 3 decimal places). Nominal length equals nominal grip plus "T" (see Sheet 1).
nominal_length_rule.note: New in this reading; the pitch_link session did not record it. It states in words that length and grip are NOT independent at nominal -- length is DEFINED as grip + T. The two are still toleranced separately (grip +/-.010, length +/-.015), so a worst-case fold that varies both independently overstates the real spread. This is the document text behind pitch_link worksheet finding F5.

cotter_hole_centerline_tolerance.text: Cotter pin hole centerline: Within .010 and normal within 2 degrees of bolt centerline.

washer_face_diameter_rule.text: Washer face diameter: Max not to exceed actual width across flats, min as tabulated.
washer_face_diameter_rule.note: Why the sheet-1 table prints only "E Dia Min": the maximum is not a number, it is a relation to the as-built hex.

thread_form.text: UNJF-3A threads per MIL-S-8879 except for reduction of thread major diameter per "TD".

at.figure: bolt side view, leader at the threaded end

thread_form.note: MIL-S-8879 is not in data/inbox/specs/. It is the document that would close the thread run-out absence below -- and MS9363 sheet 2 requirement 2 invokes the same standard for the mating nut, so one acquisition closes both sides of the joint.

material.text: 6AL-4V Titanium Alloy per AMS 4928 or AMS 4967. Locking element - Plastic per MIL-F-18240 and QPL18240.

heat_treat.text: 160 to 180 KSI ultimate tensile, 95 KSI minimum ultimate shear

bearing_surface_squareness.text: Bearing surface squareness: Within .003 TIR of shank diameter.

absences.name: thread_runout_length
absences.why: The standard dimensions grip (underside of head to the end of the full cylindrical shank, note (a)) and length (to the point), and prints T (Ref) between them, but it never dimensions the transition from full shank to full thread. Four sheets read; it is not there.
absences.closed_by: MIL-S-8879 (the thread form sheet 1 invokes) -- not in data/inbox/specs/

absences.name: thread_length
absences.why: No thread-length column and no threaded-length dimension on the sheet-1 figure. X and Y are locking-element regions (notes (g) and (h)), not the thread length.
absences.closed_by: MIL-S-8879, or the procurement specification NAS4004

entries.subject: NAS6403U11D
entries.note: Basic NAS6403 (.1900-32), unplated ("U"), grip dash 11, drilled shank ("D"). Per-basic-number values come from the sheet-1 dimension table row NAS6403; per-dash values from the sheet-3 grip/length table row 11. The part-number suffixes are what select WHICH column of sheet 1 applies -- "U" selects the unplated D-diameter column, "D" makes the optional drill P mandatory.

grip.note: The tolerance is the printed column header "Grip +/-.010", not a computed midpoint. Meaning per family value grip_definition (sheet 2 note (a)).

length.note: Not independent of grip: 1.011 - .688 = .323 = T exactly, per the family nominal_length_rule.

T_ref.note: Reference dimension (family reference_dimension_meaning). Carries no tolerance of its own.

cotter_hole_to_point.note: MEANING CONFIRMED BY THIS READING, which the pitch_link session asked a second reader to do (it could only mark M's meaning as read off the figure). On the sheet-1 figure the M dimension terminates on two extension lines: the left one is the long vertical line that runs down through the shank to the drilled cotter hole (its centerline), the right one is the point end face. So M is cotter-hole centerline to point. Rendered at Matrix(14) on the pt rect [340,108,400,185] to separate it from the neighbouring X, Y and U extension lines. The standard still never defines M in words.

cotter_hole_dia.note: Sheet-1 figure: "Drill P (j) when specified by part number chamfer optional, Csk optional". The "D" suffix is what specifies it (family part_number_code).

shank_dia.note: The "U" in the part number selects this column. The plated columns of the same row read .1887/.1881 (before) and .1895/.1885 (after) -- citing the wrong one is a silent 0.6 thou error.

thread_major_dia_reduced.note: TD is the reduced thread major diameter the figure's thread-form note excepts from MIL-S-8879.

washer_face_dia_min.note: Max is not tabulated by design -- family washer_face_diameter_rule (note (k)) makes it a relation to the as-built width across flats.

lockwire_hole_dia.note: The drilled-HEAD lockwire holes ("Drill K hole(s) within .010 of center of hex flats when specified by part number"), i.e. the "H" suffix -- NOT the shank cotter hole, which is P. NAS6403U11D has no H suffix, so this bolt has no K holes; the value is recorded because the two hole diameters are one column apart and easy to swap.

point_chamfer_U_max.note: MEANING NOT CONFIRMED. The standard never defines U in words; on the figure U is dimensioned against the point end face, beside the leader reading "Point shall be flat and chamfered. See Procurement specifications for details.", so it reads as the point chamfer/flat. Same class as M, but unlike M the extension lines do not settle it. Flagged for a third reader.

absences.name: thread_runout_length
absences.why: See the family absence of the same name. This is the element the pitch_link stack could not source and the slice-1 stack filled with an uncited 1/16 in rule of thumb.

entries.subject: NAS6404U13D
entries.note: Basic NAS6404 (.2500-28), unplated, grip dash 13, drilled shank. The VPA joint's fastener. Row 9 of the pitch_link intake queue: the document was already in the pile and this row of the table sits four rows below the one that session read.

cotter_hole_to_point.note: Same meaning as NAS6403's M, confirmed on the shared figure.

cotter_hole_dia.note: READ WITH CARE: the P cell is MERGED across the NAS6404 and NAS6405 rows and is printed on the boundary between them, so it sits visually closer to NAS6405. Confirmed at Matrix(6) on the pt rect [98,250,545,315]. R Rad .020/.010 is merged the same way.

head_fillet_radius.note: The figure labels R at the head-to-shank fillet, so this is that fillet radius; the standard does not say so in words. The NAS6403 row's R Rad cell is EMPTY -- the merged .020/.010 belongs to NAS6404 and NAS6405 only, which is why no fillet radius is recorded for NAS6403U11D.

point_chamfer_U_max.note: Meaning not confirmed -- see NAS6403U11D point_chamfer_U_max.

notes: Sheet 4 is a RESTRICTED USAGE sheet: .0156 and .0312 oversize shank bolts for repair work only, identified by an X or Y in the part number. Nothing in this repo uses one; recorded so a later reader does not mistake its D-diameter table for the sheet-1 table.
